A.explanation: Upper plate at $-320\text{ V}$ is $240\text{ V}$ below the $-80\text{ V}$ lower plate, giving the required magnitude and an upward field.

B.explanation: A potential of $-160\text{ V}$ gives only $80\text{ V}$ across $4\text{ mm}$, so $E = 20\,000\text{ V m}^{-1}$, too small.

C.explanation: A potential of $+160\text{ V}$ makes the upper plate higher than the lower plate, so the field would point downwards, not upwards.

D.explanation: A potential of $+320\text{ V}$ makes the upper plate much higher than the lower plate, giving a large downward field, opposite to that required.

hints: Notice the plate separation is $4\text{ mm} = 0.004\text{ m}$, the lower plate is fixed at $-80\text{ V}$, and the required field of $60\,000\text{ V m}^{-1}$ points upwards.
Recall for parallel plates that field magnitude is $E = V/d$, where $V$ is the magnitude of the potential difference between the plates.
Calculate $V = Ed$ in volts, then decide whether the upper plate must be higher or lower than $-80\text{ V}$ for the field to point upwards from high to low potential.
walkthrough: Identify the data: separation $d = 4\text{ mm} = 4.0 \times 10^{-3}\text{ m}$, $V_{lower} = -80\text{ V}$, and required $E = 60\,000\text{ V m}^{-1}$ upwards.
Use the uniform-field rule $E = V/d$, where $V$ is the magnitude of the potential difference, rearranged to $V = Ed$.
Substitute with units: $V = 60\,000 \times 4.0 \times 10^{-3} = 240\text{ V}$. The plates must differ by $240\text{ V}$.

Use field direction: electric field points from high potential to low potential. For the field to point upwards, potential must decrease upwards, so the upper plate must be lower than the lower plate.
Hence $V_{upper} = V_{lower} - 240 = -80 - 240 = -320\text{ V}$. This is option A.
